title: They didn’t even feel it anymore.
paragraphs: They didn’t even feel it anymore.

Not with fire.
Not with judgment.
Because the most dangerous moment in Sodom… wasn’t when sin appeared.
It was when sin stopped shocking them.
When what once whispered in the dark… started walking boldly in the streets.
And here’s the tension you can’t ignore:
What if the real warning of Sodom isn’t about them…
Because it’s easy to point at ancient cities and say, “That was wicked.”
But harder to look at our own hearts… and ask:
What have I started tolerating that God never approved?
What have I renamed just to feel comfortable?
Sin doesn’t need permission to enter your life.
It only needs your silence to stay.
You don’t even feel it anymore.
And Scripture doesn’t stay silent about this pattern.
Romans 1 says people “exchanged the truth of God for a lie” and didn’t just practice sin—they approved it (Romans 1:25, 32).
God didn’t destroy Sodom because He lost patience randomly.
Genesis 18 shows something deeper—God said the outcry against Sodom was great and their sin was “very grave.”
A culture that no longer resisted evil—but rebranded it.
Judgment doesn’t begin when God acts.
It begins when people stop responding to conviction.
Because some of us are not running from God…
we’re just slowly getting used to ignoring Him.
This is where it gets personal.
and still normalize what God is trying to convict you about on Monday.
and quietly excuse the very thing Jesus died to set you free from.
That’s spiritual compromise dressed in Christian language.
If your conviction is fading but your justification is growing…
Just a slow, steady movement away from truth.
The story of Sodom is not just about fire.
Because before Genesis 19… there was Genesis 18.
God told Abraham what He was about to do.
God knows how to rescue those who are willing to leave.
2 Peter 2:7–9 says the Lord “rescued righteous Lot… and knows how to rescue the godly from trials.”
Because this is where everything shifts.
But Jesus took the fire for us.
The judgment that should have fallen on us…
On the cross, God didn’t ignore sin.
Isaiah 53 says He was “pierced for our transgressions” and “crushed for our iniquities.”
So grace is not God pretending sin is okay.
Grace is God paying for it Himself.
You don’t have to normalize sin to survive it.
You can be freed from it.
If your version of grace allows you to stay in what Jesus died to break…
You are not too far gone.
Because the same God who judged Sodom…
sent His Son to save sinners.
You are not called to blend in with darkness.
You are called to be set apart in truth.
You are not a prisoner of your patterns.
You are a redeemed soul with a new nature in Christ.
Come back to Jesus—not halfway, not casually, but fully.
It’s the doorway back to life.
Because the next message might be the one that pulls someone out of their “Sodom.”
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
